items.title: Luther Henderson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Honi Coles, the tap dancer. [INTERVIEWEE] And the group, what's the group? [Billie Henderson] Copacetics [INTERVIEWEE] Copacetics. They either taught us a routine or did a routine.

ctx.x: Can you say that for me one more time?

The Personality Eight Merry Makers. Now you ask Mercer about this. (chuckles) He was one of the chief ones. Anyway, we hired one of the most popular bands to play a dance at the Renaissance Casino. And the leader of that band was Charlie Barnett. And we were … 'cause he had just put out Cherokee; it was a big arrangement at the time. And I don't know, but we may possibly have been, if not the first, one of the first black organizations to hire a white jazz band to come play in Harlem. That's an interesting…
